description.narrative: The Government through the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) used the disability module in the Labour Force Survey (LFS) in 2022. The last quarterly report of the LFS in 2023 will include a chapter focusing on the disability data. ILO assisted the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) in developing a workplan over the reporting period through numerous consultations to improve the BBS's capacity to collect, analyse, and report sex and disability disaggregated data from the Labour Force Survey (LFS) in the specific disability module. BBS officials attended a technical seminar on the revised definitions of the International Conference on Labour Statistics (ICLS) for the analysis and reporting of labour market indicators in the LFS 2022. Since this is the first time the BBS developed a report for the LFS's disability module, the ILO provided a sample reporting structure, essential reporting indicators, and instructions for creating the report.

description.narrative: The government of Bangladesh has adopted a revised National Action Plan (NAP) to eliminate child labour in Bangladesh for 2021-25 in December 2021. The government of Bangladesh has also formed a National Child Labour Welfare Council (NCLWC) headed by the Labour Minister to guide the implementation of the NPA in coordination with other relevant 18 ministries. The government of Bangladesh has also updated the Hazardous Child Labour List emphasising eliminating it in a strategic approach. Piloted a Community-Based Child Labour Monitoring System (CLMS) model targeting a sub-district through a holistic approach by identifying the children working in hazardous work, making necessary linkages for children to be withdrawn from hazardous work for their return to school and/or find employment in non-hazardous forms of work, and also linking the children’s families with available social safety net programmes with support from local government authorities and representatives, as necessary. As a member of the drafting committee, ILO contributed significantly to revise the NPA. ILO also contributed to the formation and functioning of the NCLWS. The ILO provided inputs as a member of the technical committee formed by the Government to update the hazardous child labour list. With the funding of FCDO, ILO has been implementing the pilot CLMS with a Non-government organization since August 2022 and the process of integrating it into the government system.
